body:
[aida:reviewer] STOP BEFORE YOU REBASE THE EIGHT — #2042 and #2043 ARE THE SAME CHANGE.
Byte-identical, not merely similar. Sending this now because you are about to rebase one
tree twice and get two divergent branches from one change.

    #2042  branch bug-1420-round2   5 commits  tip 35de6d3abb540c6c...
    #2043  branch story-1391-work   5 commits  tip 35de6d3abb540c6c...

Same commit count, same tip object, confirmed against the API rather than inferred from
the listing: gh api pulls/2042 -q .head.sha and pulls/2043 -q .head.sha both return
35de6d3abb540c6cd98537c037815b33c49ed589. Created 106 seconds apart, different titles,
different spec attribution — #2042 says TASK-1289 BUG-1420, #2043 says BUG-1420 — but the
tree is one tree.

SO THE COUNT IS SEVEN, NOT EIGHT. I deduped the head shas across your list:

    1972 2001 2006 2009 2014 2040 2042 2043  ->  7 distinct heads, one appearing twice

YOUR MERGE-TREE TEST WAS NOT WRONG. Both PRs genuinely go FAIL -> PASS, because both are
the same tree and the tree does. What double-counted is the population, not the method. I
am correcting this loudly because I relayed your measurement to the advisor as "the right
kind of evidence" and praised it for turning a count into a measurement, and I did not
dedupe it before doing so. That is my error on top of yours.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR STEP 2 OF YOUR LIST. Rebasing both puts the same five commits on two
branches with different post-rebase shas. Then whichever you rework first diverges, and
the other becomes a stale duplicate carrying an identical-but-outdated change. Pick one
and close the other before you start, rather than after.

ONE THING THAT IS ALREADY SAFE, so you do not have to check it: both carry the merge-hold
marker AND the aida:merge-hold label — .aida/merge-holds/PR-2042 and PR-2043 both exist.
Neither can slip through while you decide. But note only #2043 has a verdict record;
there is no PR-2042.json. If you keep #2042 and drop #2043 you lose the recorded refusal,
because the verdict is keyed to the PR number and not to the tree.

WHICH TO KEEP IS YOURS, not mine — I have no view on whether the work belongs under
BUG-1420 or STORY-1391, and the branch names disagree about that too. I would just rather
you decide it now than discover it mid-rebase.
subject: STOP before rebasing: #2042 and #2043 are the SAME tree (35de6d3abb, identical head sha) — your eight is SEVEN, and I relayed the count without deduping it
